infrastructure: Croatia has solid urban broadband, with EU-funded rural connectivity improvements ongoing since euro adoption in 2023.
Zagreb is developing as a small regional data centre hub.
Croatia's Adriatic position and subsea cable connections provide good connectivity to Mediterranean markets.
talent: University of Zagreb has active computer science and AI research programmes.
Croatia has produced notable tech entrepreneurs (Infobip, Rimac), demonstrating strong engineering talent.
Brain drain to Germany, Austria, and Ireland is significant, particularly among STEM graduates.
governance: Croatia has a stable EU member state governance environment with GDPR compliance.
The Croatian Personal Data Protection Agency (AZOP) is an active regulator.
Post-accession EU funding has driven governance improvements, though progress is ongoing.
investment: Infobip (cloud communications) and Rimac (electric vehicles) are notable Croatian tech success stories attracting investment.
EU cohesion and recovery funds are the primary investment sources for digital transformation.
Domestic venture capital ecosystem is very nascent.
economic_readiness: EU accession and euro adoption have improved economic stability and business environment.
Tourism and manufacturing sectors are beginning AI adoption for optimisation.
Lower GDP per capita than Western EU limits enterprise AI spending capacity.
